# Feature: one routing-outcome line per request

Parent: LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE. Depends on: LP children "local-preferred pin across every local-route exit", "deferral — queue-budget expiry yields a retryable 429" and "too-large promotion — local stripped from the effective chain" (each stamps its outcome).

## Goal

Every request emits exactly **one** log line naming the resolved preference and whether it was pinned to local, deferred, promoted to remote (or served/exhausted), so an operator can tell a deferral from chain exhaustion without correlating per-skip lines — and a legacy `local-only` request is reported under its normalised value.

## Deliverables

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`:
  - A single emission point on the top-level return path — `_stamp_local_route_headers()` (~:6608), which both entries (`proxy_with_fallback` :12550, `proxy_with_remote_fallback` :10455) already call exactly once after `_run_chain_cycles()` — emitting:
    `local_preference_resolved preference=<resolved> outcome=<pinned|deferred|promoted|local|remote|exhausted> reason=<token|none> session=<id> model=<name>`
  - Outcome stamped on the request at the existing decision points: pin refusal (`pinned`), deferral refusal (`deferred`), pre-loop strip (`promoted`), local success (`local`), remote success (`remote`), exhaustion (`exhausted`). A request that resolves `prefer-local`/`remote-ok` reports the preference verbatim with the actual serving outcome.
  - Emission is best-effort (`try/except`, `logger.info`) and must never raise or mutate the response; it must be outside the per-cycle loop so a chain-hold retry (multiple `_run_chain_cycles` iterations) still produces exactly one line.
  - The resolved preference is the **normalised** value already cached on the request (`request._local_preference`), so `local-only` prints as `local-preferred` (alias parity with LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16).
- Tests (`proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` and/or `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`):
  - `caplog` assertions per outcome: local served, pinned refusal, deferred refusal, promoted remote, `prefer-local` remote fall-through, legacy `local-only` → normalised line. Each asserts **count == 1** for the line, its preference field, its outcome field and its reason token.
  - A multi-cycle chain-hold case asserting still exactly one line.
- Comments/docstring at `_stamp_local_route_headers()` describing the single-emission contract and why the outcome is stamped rather than logged at each branch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 Exactly one `local_preference_resolved` line per request on every outcome — asserted with `caplog` for: local served, pinned refusal, deferred refusal, promoted remote, `prefer-local` remote success and exhaustion (count == 1 each).
- AC2 The line names the **resolved** preference and the outcome (`pinned` / `deferred` / `promoted` / `local` / `remote` / `exhausted`) plus the canonical reason token when one exists, so a deferral (`outcome=deferred reason=fallback_after_queue`) is unambiguously distinguishable from chain exhaustion (`outcome=exhausted`) — the parent-epic log requirement (LP-0MVNTJQVB007QWEZ) and never "All providers exhausted" for a deferral (LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ).
- AC3 A legacy `X-Local-Preference: local-only` request logs `preference=local-preferred` and never presents `local-only` as the resolved value (alias parity; the once-per-request deprecation warning from LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 is unchanged and separate).
- AC4 Emission cannot change behaviour: a test asserts the response status, headers and body are identical with the line suppressed, and that an exception inside the emission (patched logger) still returns the response unchanged.
- AC5 Exactly one line even when `_run_chain_cycles()` performs multiple chain-hold cycles for one request.
- AC6 No competing per-skip outcome lines: the existing `priority_routing`, `local_admission_guard`, `contention_queue_*` and `local_only_refused` lines are left as they are (asserted unchanged), and no new line is emitted inside either dispatch loop.
- AC7 (parent AC7) All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and docstrings; operator-facing docs (`docs/`, `proxy/config.yaml` commentary) are tracked in LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57.
- AC8 (parent AC8) Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (changed-scope gate first; the full suite is enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- One line per **request**, not per cycle, per skip branch or per refusal builder.
- No new observability vocabulary: outcome values are a small closed set defined beside the existing preference constants (or in `provider.py` next to the refusal helpers); reason tokens come from the existing canonical table.
- No metrics/OTel/HTTP-header addition — log line only.
- Best-effort and side-effect free: observability must never break or alter a response.
- Scope guard: no refusal-line redesign (LP-0MVRMC275000R2W6 owns the refusal lines), no operator docs (LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57).

## Existing state (verified during planning)

- `_stamp_local_route_headers(response, request, model_config)` at `proxy/provider.py:6608` — the existing single choke point on the top-level return path (docstring: "Single choke point on the top-level return path so local success, remote success, refusal and exhaustion are all covered"). It delegates to `admission_reserve.stamp_route_headers()` and reads `request._local_fallback_reason`; a response already carrying `X-Local-Route` is left untouched. Both entries call it once after `_run_chain_cycles()` (:10488 `proxy_with_remote_fallback`, :12583 `proxy_with_fallback`), so it is the only place where exactly-once emission is structural.
- `request._local_preference` is the cached normalised preference (set by `provider._request_local_preference()` / `priority.local_preference_for_request()`); `request._local_fallback_reason` is the canonical reason token stamped by `_note_local_fallback_reason()`.
- `_run_chain_cycles(request, path, model_config, config, cycle_fn)` (:9797) runs chain-hold retry cycles, which is why per-cycle logging would duplicate.
- Existing per-request lines an operator already correlates: `priority_routing ... preference=<pref>` (both cycles), `local_admission_guard decision=... reason=...`, `contention_queue_wait`/`contention_queue_dispatch`/`contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`, `local_only_refused reason=<token> preference=...` (`_log_local_only_refusal()` ~:6505).
- Tests today assert on those lines with `caplog` in `test_routing_preference_logging.py` (786 lines) — the natural home for the new-line assertions alongside `test_local_admission_guard.py`.

## Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — outcome stamping in both cycles plus the refusal paths, `_stamp_local_route_headers()` emission, outcome vocabulary constants, docstrings.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — consumed only: preference constants for the resolved value.
- `proxy/tests/test_routing_preference_logging.py` — `caplog` assertions for the new line (per outcome, once per request, alias normalisation).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — one-line-per-request assertion on the refusal rows (exactly one, not one per branch).

## Dependency graph (wired 2026-10-28)

- Depends on: LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2 (pin), LP-0MVSM06BK008FZUE (deferral), LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4 (too-large promotion) — each stamps the outcome this child reads.
- No dependents: LP-0MVSHXTX1007D58Z / LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57 (tests, docs) consume the implemented behaviour, not this line.
